The test image shows a soybean stem with prominent pink/lavender discoloration along its length, with scattered reddish spots. Leaves in the background appear mostly green and healthy. This is a stem disease.

Top candidates: Phytophthora (stem rot), Rhizoctonia (stem lesions), Fusarium (pink stem), Phomopsis (stem cankers).

Let me check reference images one at a time.
Not a match — Phytophthora shows brown wilted plant. Now checking Fusarium.
This has some reddish stem discoloration but localized at base. Checking Phomopsis.
Not matching. Checking Anthracnose (stem canker symptoms).
Anthracnose shows dried brown stems with black dots — not matching. The pink/lavender live stem in the test image points toward Cercospora (which causes purple stem discoloration). Checking it.
Cercospora_107 shows leaf spots. I need to see if Cercospora has stem symptoms, and also check Phytophthora stem view. 2 views left.
Cercospora shows seed purple stain and leaf spots. Now for my final view, checking Phytophthora stem reference.

**Analysis summary:**

- Test image: soybean stem with pink/lavender/purple discoloration along its length, with scattered small reddish spots. Leaves are mostly green (plant still alive).
- Phytophthora: brown wilted plants — no match
- Fusarium: curled wilting stem tip — no match
- Rhizoctonia: localized reddish-brown lesion at base — partial but different location
- Phomopsis: pod/seed white mold — no match
- Anthracnose: dried brown stems with black dots — no match
- Cercospora: shows leaf spots and purple seed stain; the pathogen (C. kikuchii) is well known to also cause **purple stem blight** — pink/lavender discoloration along stems with reddish speckling, exactly matching the test image
- Phytophthora_27: young plants with leaf spots, no pink stem — no match

The distinctive pink/lavender stem coloration on an otherwise still-living plant with small reddish spots is the classic presentation of Cercospora blight (C. kikuchii purple stem discoloration). No other checked class showed this pattern.
